# 1 Enoch Chapter 67 — Disagreement Log
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

## 67:1 — 'your lot has come up before me' — Noah addressed directly

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "thy-lot has-come-up before-me" | Archaic second person; literal |
| LOGOS | "your lot has come up before me" | Modern; 'lot' preserved |
| PNEUMA | "your case has come before me" | 'Case' for 'lot' — forensic metaphor |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. 'Your lot has come up before me' uses the idiom of a judicial lot-casting — Noah's case has been presented and adjudicated. PNEUMA's 'case' is accurate but loses the specific lot/allotment imagery.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 67:2 — 'wooden structure' vs. 'wooden building' for the ark

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "wooden-[building]" | Bracketed; 'building' supplied |
| LOGOS | "wooden structure" | 'Structure' is neutral and appropriate |
| PNEUMA | "wooden vessel" | Explicitly identifies it as the ark |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS's 'wooden structure.' The Ge'ez does not specify 'vessel' (PNEUMA) or 'building' (EMET) — 'structure' is the most neutral. PNEUMA's 'vessel' is interpretively correct (this is clearly the ark) but the text maintains some ambiguity that SOPHIA preserves.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---

## 67:8 — body healed / spirit punished — the paradox of the hot springs

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "for-the-healing-of-the-body, but-for-the-punishment-of-the-spirit" | Literal antithesis |
| LOGOS | "for the healing of the body, but for the punishment of the spirit" | Preserves the antithesis |
| PNEUMA | "healing their bodies while punishing their spirits" | Participial construction; same content |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. The antithetical structure ('for X, but for Y') is more sharply expressed in LOGOS's rendering. This is the theological heart of the chapter and the antithesis should be preserved clearly.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS. Theological antithesis preserved.

---

## 67:12 — Michael's testimony speech

| Translator | Rendering | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| EMET | "This-judgment-wherewith-the-angels-are-judged-is-a-testimony-for-the-kings" | Literal; 'testimony' carries evidential weight |
| LOGOS | "This judgment with which the angels are judged is a testimony for the kings" | Agrees |
| PNEUMA | "This judgment by which the angels are judged is itself a testimony for the kings" | Adds 'itself' for emphasis |

**SOPHIA's resolution:** Adopted LOGOS. 'A testimony' (Ge'ez se'atat = witness, testimony) is precise — the angels' punishment is intended to serve as evidence/witness for the kings' judgment. PNEUMA's addition of 'itself' is unnecessary.

**Status:** Resolved in favor of LOGOS.

---
